pairs.why: Both are flat wall clocks very close to the real one; A's rim is very slightly softer and less saturated, so it edges ahead by a small margin.
A is mounted flat on the striped wall like the real clock, while B stands on a floor ledge with a cast shadow, which changes the staging.
A is flush on the wall like the real card, while B is set on the ground with a floor shadow and so doesn't match the real composition.
B is the wall-mounted clock that matches the real card's staging, while A stands on a floor with a shadow underneath.
A is a fully built, painterly open coffin set into the scene with calmer wood tones like the real cards, while B is a flat, glossy, overly orange upright slab.
A reads as a real clear glass ball on a solid gold stand, like the real drink glass, while B's swirling magic glow and curly stand look more like generic fantasy-icon art.
B has rivets, banded seams, an exhaust nozzle and fuller fins, which matches how carefully the real submarine and trumpet are built, while A is a simpler, plasticky toy shape.
A's softer, matte teal saucer is closer to the real cards' soft toy-like finish, while B's shiny chrome body is glossier than the real cards.
